title: New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar Is Not Tahrir Square, But It Can Become One
author: Asif Ullah Khan
text:
Protestors gather at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, India, July 21, 2026.
Credit: X/Cockroach is Back
It is tempting to compare the students’ protest at New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar with Cairo’s Tahrir Square, the epicenter of the uprising that brought to an end Hosni Mubarak’s nearly 30-year rule.The comparison, however, is only partly valid. Equating what is happening in New Delhi with Egypt’s iconic protest would be unrealistic, even if the two movements share striking similarities. In Egypt, calls to gather at Tahrir Square spread rapidly through social media, including YouTube and Facebook. Likewise, the Cockroach Janta Party, which emerged on Instagram, has used social media to mobilize thousands to assemble at Jantar Mantar and protest against the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) examination paper leak, which has fueled widespread anger among students and, according to the movement, contributed to a tragic wave of student suicides.[...]
